prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro CBTC (Communications-Based Train Control) System: separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. LTC declares degraded mode when MA, localization, points, platform interface or radio untrusted (loss of trust treated as loss of comms); trains stop or run at controlled speed. Return to automatic needs stable comms, verified routes, confirmed positions, recorded maintenance-to-operations handback; cybersecurity controls are prerequisites. Safety-critical faults stay under traffic control until LTC and Maple confirm; evidence frozen to protected repository; configuration versions recorded. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC): monitors Lantern, no vital intervention; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; receives Route Release Exception List; starts manual route recovery confirming positions by independent indications and verbal reports; resets affecting routes/occupancy need LTC+Maple concurrence. Revenue Train Operator: acknowledges to Atlas; restricted manual authorized via Voice Dispatch Console unless contingency comms invoked; repeats back limit, max speed, stopping point, platform-clear instruction; sends Test Train Clearance Memo after proving run. Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple: remote read-only outside window; verifies points, vacancy, local protection before manual route; Axle Counter Reset Request is controlling authority to restore failed section. Cyber Security Officer: reviews authentication failures, lockouts, abnormal access. Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: shows limits, fallback mode, pending actions without obscuring alarms; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas. Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: read-only; checks Brake Curve Checksum Log; tags sessions with incident ID before restart. North District Zone Controller, alias Marble: applies Temporary Speed Restriction Notice after validation. South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid: inhibits auto routing in blocks under manual confirmation. Both send MA to Atlas. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon: Axle Counter Reset Request; holds points locked until confirmation. West Junction Interlocking: sends Route Release Exception List to LTC; rejects routes conflicting with manual moves. Interlockings are final vital authority. Platform Screen Door Controller: Platform Door Status Snapshot; protected local state if stopping unverified. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout, restricted manual; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer flags uncertain location. Train Radio Modem reports safe-data loss to Atlas. Wayside Radio Access Network: reduce throughput first. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance: no bypass unless emergency procedure. Passenger Information Gateway: messages match LTC limits.

New part:
S202: The Cyber Security Officer shall maintain continuous monitoring of security events from the Safety Data Communication Network, the Wayside Radio Access Network, and the Metro Operations Control System.
S203: Security monitoring shall correlate authentication failures, session resets, rejected messages, configuration changes, and abnormal timing patterns without altering any safety command path.
S204: Alerts affecting train control availability shall be classified using operational impact, affected territory, and whether the event could change train movement authority.
S205: The Line Traffic Controller shall be notified when a cybersecurity event requires a restriction on automatic operation or a change in communications mode.
S206: The Cyber Security Officer uses the audit file to investigate radio session continuity and to confirm that security monitoring records are complete.
S207: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall be the controlled source for operational certificates used by trainborne, wayside, control center, and maintenance components.
S208: Certificate issuance shall require approved asset identity, recorded software baseline, assigned operating domain, and confirmation that the requesting component is authorized for service.
S209: Certificate renewal shall be planned before expiry so that the Atlas Onboard Controller, Train Radio Modem, North District Zone Controller, South District Zone Controller, and West Junction Interlocking do not enter service with degraded trust.
S210: Falcon shall reject any control message with an invalid signature, an expired certificate, or a sequence value outside the accepted window.
S211: Revocation shall be available for a compromised device, a retired device, or a device whose maintenance history can no longer be reconciled with approved configuration records.
S212: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server shall not be used to bypass certificate checks or to create alternate trust paths into safety-related communications.
S213: Administrative access to the Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall require named accounts, multifactor authentication, separation of duties, and recorded approval for privileged changes.
S214: The Signal Maintenance Engineer may request access needed for fault isolation, but the Cyber Security Officer shall approve security-sensitive permissions before they are enabled.
S215: The Revenue Train Operator shall not be assigned cybersecurity administration duties during passenger service, although security warnings presented in the cab shall remain part of normal operating awareness.
S216: The Metro Operations Control System uses the Test Train Clearance Memo as a controlled prerequisite before accepting security exceptions for non-revenue movement in protected territory.
S217: Audit evidence shall include time-synchronized event records, access approvals, certificate actions, configuration changes, alarm acknowledgements, and operator instructions related to communications security.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
